lyrics:
[Intro: harmonica riff, big drums, slide guitar]

[Verse 1: bright male tenor, driving]
Dashboard says we'll make it by three
If we never stop, never eat, never see
A single thing but the bumper ahead
Kid in the back seat looks up and says

[Chorus: shouted group vocal, full band]
Take the scenic route!
World's biggest ball of twine, here we come
Take the scenic route!
Pie at a diner and a river to jump
We got all day and a tank of gas
The fast way's faster but it don't last
Take the scenic route!

[Verse 2: tenor, guitars chugging]
My old man drove like a man on the run
Elbow out the window, never stopped once
I saw this whole country at seventy-five
Turns out it's prettier at forty, with the windows wide

[Chorus: shouted group vocal, full band]
Take the scenic route!
World's biggest ball of twine, here we come
Take the scenic route!
Pie at a diner and a river to jump
We got all day and a tank of gas
The fast way's faster but it don't last
Take the scenic route!

[Bridge: half-time, harmonica and voice]
Nobody at the end ever wished they'd made good time
They wish they'd pulled over at the lemonade sign

[Final Chorus: key lift, everything louder]
Take the scenic route!
World's biggest ball of twine, here we come
Take the scenic route!
Pie at a diner and a river to jump
We got all day and a tank of gas
The fast way's faster but it don't last
Take the scenic route!

[Outro: harmonica, a child and a father, spoken]
Are we there yet?
Not even close.
Good.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 104 BPM, 4/4, F major, lifting to G major for the last chorus. A big, sunny, rolling drive.

VOICE: Male tenor, bright, high and clean, with stacked harmonies. A group shouts the title line each time. A child speaks in the outro and he answers.

INSTRUMENTS: Harmonica riff, slide guitar, chugging electric guitars, strummed acoustic guitar, bass, a loud live drum kit, organ pad, tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, harmonica and drums. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:36 Chorus 1. 1:04 Verse 2. 1:28 Chorus 2. 1:56 Bridge, half-time. 2:16 Final chorus, key up. 2:46 Outro, harmonica and three spoken lines, ends 3:16.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2000s country-rock for a film soundtrack: loud, glossy, wide guitars, vocals bright.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The child's 'Good' at the very end, 3:12.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original wants to drive it all, fast. This one has learned from a father who never stopped, and lets a child set the pace.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Hurrying, interrupted, converted, in no rush.
